column3: The Hebrew speaks of their soothing odors without explicitly naming sacrifices in this verse; BSB adds “of your sacrifices.”
The Hebrew uses singular collective “their heart” and says the leaf’s sound will “pursue” them; BSB uses plural “their hearts” and says the sound will “put them to flight.”
The Hebrew says each will stumble over “his brother”; BSB uses “one another.”
The Hebrew repeats the wasting-away verb and includes “with them”; BSB varies it with “decay” and omits that phrase.
The Hebrew joins the confession with “and”; BSB introduces it conditionally with “But if.”

The Hebrew uses future “I will walk” and “I will bring”; BSB gives past “I acted” and “brought.” The Hebrew also has singular collective “their uncircumcised heart,” rendered as plural “hearts” in BSB.
The Hebrew uses the remembering verb three times; BSB states it twice.
The Hebrew makes “their soul” the subject of abhorring the statutes; BSB uses “they.”
The Hebrew says “before the eyes of the nations”; BSB uses “in the sight of the nations.”
The Hebrew says the LORD “gave” these laws “by the hand of Moses”; BSB says He “established” them “through Moses.”
